notes.title: PANIC High Newsletter #4: Patch 3, widescreen, and Google Play Store!
notes.notes:
Hello prospective and current students of Multiverse High!

I know that you’re ready to head off to a joyous summer vacation, and probably wondering what I’m doing making an announcement. But I’ve got wonderful news, so get ready…

[i]PANIC at Multiverse High![/i] is now WIDESCREEN! No longer shackled to the square screen of old, the game is now in glorious 1920 x 1080 resolution! Now you can see the full glorious backgrounds by the talented Rachel Dorrett, larger versions of the characters by the amazing Sarah Bergh, and objects and critters by the incomparable Michelle Juett Silva! 

AND THAT ISN’T ALL. Our embarrassment of artistic riches has spilled over into the rewards of the Gallery and Yearbook – now when you unlock an entry, you can access extra art! Yearbook characters will have a sheet of full body poses (so you can actually see their feet! GASP!), as well as some excellent pixel animation courtesy of the fantastic Paul “Doomcube” Conway. Gallery pages will include their own secrets, including more pixel work, rough sketches, and initial art passes!

All of this is wrapped in a bright and shiny new UI, redesigned to be more comely both on computers and – this is a big one – easily usable on mobile devices. That’s right – in addition to having its one true home here on Steam, [i]PANIC at Multiverse High![/i] can now be found on the Google Play store. Think of it as your way to “learn on the go”!

As always, if you have any comments or questions for us here at Multiverse High, we’d be delighted to hear them, and welcome you to make your voice heard. In the meantime, and as always, we wish you an exciting year!

Happy Learning!

Annie VanderMeer Mitsoda
Principal (Project Lead)

notes.title: Dead State Dev s Panic At Multiverse High! Gets Demo
notes.notes:
Panic at Multiverse High! [official site] has been out for over a month already, but now you can try before you buy in a new demo. It’s Dead State developer DoubleBear’s take on a dating sim set in a high school where things are a bit… off.

Things start out normally enough. Canned music straight out of a ’90s job training video check. A school bully named Chad check. Said school bully is pink and has six arms well, hold on.

… [visit site to read more]

notes.title: PANIC High Newsletter #3: Patch 2, enrollment open for Mac and Linux users, and DEMO READY!
notes.notes:
Hello again, current and future denizens of Multiverse High! I have multiple exciting news tidbits for you today, so buckle in!

First of all, I'm delighted to announce that our poor neglected Mac and Linux-using prospective students are now no longer neglected. That's right - Mac and Linux compatibility is GO! Thanks to the diligence and patience of our most excellent testers, our school should now be open to even more potential students. Hooray!

Secondly, to those of you who aren't quite sure about enrolling fully in Multiverse High, we're pleased to offer a "starter course" if you will - that is to say, we've got a DEMO ready! Try it out to see the cast of our six amazing school clubs, and a bit of content in some of our classes. We hope you enjoy what you see and are eager to find out more!

As a side comment, please, if you're enjoying your time at Multiverse High, why not leave a review to tell others what you thought? Or if you have some comments and thoughts of things you would like to see improved, or questions or somesuch, please hop onto our Discussion section to let us know what's on your mind! Many and sincere thanks to all who've contributed to both so far, and we hope to hear from you again in the future.

That's all the time we have for now, but thank you to all those enrolled so far, and we hope you're having an exciting and fruitful year.

Happy Learning!

Annie VanderMeer Mitsoda
Principal (Project Lead)

notes.title: PANIC High Newsletter #2: First Patch is go!
notes.notes:
Hello again, current students (and possibly future interested attendees)!

Today we celebrate not only the two-week-a-versary (I tried looking up if this had a proper Latin name, but the Goobluz search engine was NO HELP) of the beginning of school here at Multiverse High! We’ve been very pleased to see your happy faces in the halls (although every day we seem to see less and less Kevins – are you cutting class, young men?) and hope to see more promising young folks join our ranks.

We’re pleased to also offer up our very first “Patch”! I have been told this is a fascinating bit of technology that presents fixes to issues large and small. How lovely! Our excellent technology officer has given me a list of some things that have been dealt with:

+ A number of typos have been fixed, thanks to the diligence of multiple students in pointing them out! Thank you for your conscientiousness!

+ “Self-voicing” mechanic will now not repeatedly read the date. Although it is always prudent to be mindful of one’s scheduling, constant reminders bordering on nagging are never any fun!

+ Minor visual errors have been fixed (likely thanks to Art Club!)

A quick apology to students from the Mac and Linux departments that we do not yet have versions ready for you, but rest assured that our whole faculty is working very hard on the problem, and are being assisted by some truly kind and hardworking individuals. Your help today makes a better tomorrow!

That’s it for me for now, but I do hope you check back in with us for future exciting updates. Be sure to tell everyone about the fun you have at Multiverse High – we always welcome new enrollees! 

Happy Learning!

Annie VanderMeer Mitsoda
Principal (Project Lead)

notes.title: Welcome to Multiverse High!
notes.notes:
Greetings future denizens, current students, and past alumni of Multiverse High!

It's a grand day today as we finally open the doors to this secret project we've been hush-hush about for a while. We thank you kindly for joining us (or at least for your interest in our fine institution), and wanted to notify you of one critical announcement: unfortunately, prospective students who are seeking a Mac and/or a Linux version will not have that option currently. However, these are definitely versions that myself and other members of the faculty ARE considering, so fear not! You are being considered.

As always, if there any issues with your registration, there are staff members on our Discussion who are eager to provide assistance. Simply post and we will do our best to get to you as speedily as possible!

Finally, we should like to give credit to two members of our staff who were kind enough to devote their time and energy towards this delightful enterprise, and we thought we should give them a brief shout-out:

+ Michelle Juett Silva, esteemed half (and Art Unicorn) of Ska Studios, who contributed artwork to the game. Check out their own works, a lovely savage tale called [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/283640/][i]Salt and Sanctuary[/i][/url]. Very nice! 

+ Lena Raine, who composed the delightful chiptune themes you hear throughout our sainted halls. If you wish your own copy of her fantastic works, you may [url=https://radicaldreamland.bandcamp.com/album/panic-at-multiverse-high]find it here[/url]: 

Alas, that's all the time we have for today. Thank you again for thinking of your friends, faculty, and fellow students here at Multiverse High, and we do wish you a most fruitful and exciting day.

Happy Learning!

Annie VanderMeer Mitsoda
Principal (Project Lead)
